Copies requested for any other federal or State needs-based benefit or program
feeRules: A custodian may impose a charge that is no more than a flat $5.00 fee or no more than $0.50 per page, whichever is greater (18 V.S.A. § 9419(a))

A custodian may charge an individual a fee, reasonably related to the associated costs, for providing copies of X-rays, films, models, disks, tapes, or other health care record information maintained in other formats (18 V.S.A. § 9419(b))

provisions.title: Charges for access to medical records
provisions.quote: A custodian shall not charge for providing copies of any health care record requested to support a claim or an appeal under any provision of the Social Security Act or for any other federal or State needs-based benefit or program.
provisions.appliesTo: “Custodian” means any person who maintains health care information for any lawful purpose, including a health care provider, a health care facility, or a health insurer.

copy_rights.note: Free copy for Social Security and needs-based benefit claims goes beyond HIPAA and Part 171. No day deadline found; 26 V.S.A. § 1354(a)(10) says only promptly. The $5 or $0.50 per page fee is a fact, not counted.

crossCheck.note: beyondFederalFloor yes: free copy for benefit claims is not in HIPAA or Part 171. Current text from 2017 Act 113 (Adj. Sess.), effective July 1, 2018. No day deadline found; 26 V.S.A. 1354(a)(10) says promptly. No 2026 amendment.

hiv.note: Covers public health agency records on HIV or AIDS. Subsection (d) bars disclosure or discovery in any civil, criminal or administrative proceeding.

provisions.title: Genetic testing; limitations
provisions.quote: any results of genetic testing or the fact that an individual has requested genetic services or undergone genetic testing shall be disclosed only pursuant to a written authorization executed by the individual tested or by a person authorized by law to act for the individual.

genetic.note: Disclosure of genetic test results needs written authorization. Subsection (d) requires written authorization and informed consent before testing.

facts.statutoryDamages: Genetic testing: civil damages including punitive damages, costs and attorney's fees (18 V.S.A. § 9335(b)). HIV or other public health records: actual damages; civil penalty $10,000 to $25,000 for willful disclosure; up to $2,500 paid to the subject for negligent disclosure (18 V.S.A. § 1001(e)).

provisions.title: Genetic testing; remedies
provisions.quote: Any person aggrieved by a violation of this chapter may bring an action for civil damages, including punitive damages, equitable relief, including restraint of prohibited acts, restitution of wages or other benefits, and reinstatement, costs, and reasonable attorney’s fees, and other appropriate relief.

provisions.title: Confidential public health records; liability
provisions.quote: Commits any act described in subdivision (1), (2), or (3) of this subsection shall be liable to the subject for all actual damages, including damages for any economic, bodily, or psychological harm that is a proximate result of the act.

private_right.note: Suits limited to genetic testing and confidential public health records such as HIV. 18 V.S.A. § 1881 has no private right. Act 145 of 2026, Sec. 2, states an intent to give no private right under the new privacy act.

crossCheck.note: Suits cover genetic tests and public health records only. 18 V.S.A. 1881 has none. Act 145 Sec. 2 declines a private right. Act 156 gives consumer protection suits for AI mental health services, not records.
